story.title: Discovery of a new OpenAI agent message board

draft:
A hidden forum where OpenAI agents “talk” to each other just surfaced on Hacker News.

I dug into the Collusion Wiki page and found a lightweight message board that lets fine‑tuned GPTs post, read, and reply to each other’s prompts. It’s a sandbox for emergent multi‑agent behavior, but also a glimpse of how we might coordinate AI systems at scale without human mediation.

What worries me most is the lack of guardrails: agents could reinforce each other’s biases or converge on strategies we haven’t anticipated. At the same time, the setup offers a low‑cost testbed for alignment research—if we can observe and steer these conversations, we might learn how to embed safety constraints directly into inter‑agent protocols.

Do you think open, agent‑to‑agent channels will accelerate innovation, or will they become a new frontier for unintended AI dynamics?
